Sources: [mixMC HMP case study](https://mixomics.org/mixmc/hmp-bodysites-case-study/),
[PLSDAbatch](https://evayiwenwang.github.io/PLSDAbatch_workflow/),
Nygaard et al. 2016 *Biostatistics* (batch correction and inflated group effects).

# Analysis plan

::: {.callout-important}
## Read this first: n = 20

With 20 samples and ~4000 ASVs, every supervised model can separate groups perfectly
**on the training data**. Results only count when they hold up in cross-validation **and**
beat a permutation null. Every supervised step below has both.
:::

| # | Step | Question | Method | How `run` is handled | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sequencing depth | Is depth adequate and is it linked to run or District? | Library sizes, rarefaction curves, rarefaction slope, depth vs PC1 | Depth tested against run | Keep/drop decision |
| 2 | Design check | Can run and District be separated at all? | Run × District table, Cramér's V, env vars vs run | – | Go/no-go for correction |
| 3 | Preprocessing | – | Filter rare ASVs, CLR (pseudocount 1) | – | `clr_raw` |
| 4 | Batch effect | How much variance is run? Does correction remove it without removing District? | PCA, PERMANOVA, variance partitioning, silhouette; `limma::removeBatchEffect` vs per-run centering (vs PLSDA-batch) | Corrected matrix `X_bc` | Chosen correction |
| 5 | NMDS | Do samples group by District, run, shortName? | NMDS on Bray–Curtis (raw) and Aitchison (raw and corrected); PERMANOVA, betadisper, envfit | Run as a PERMANOVA term; permutations within run | Ordination figures + tests |
| 6 | sPLS-DA (District) | Which ASVs discriminate Districts? | Tuned sPLS-DA, repeated CV, permutation test, leave-one-run-out | Corrected CLR; permutations redo the correction | BER, selected ASVs (Order-Genus) |
| 7 | sPLS regression (pH, DO, Temp, Ammonia) | Can the community predict each variable, and which ASVs drive it? | sPLS1 per variable, LOO-CV Q², permutation test, VIP; RDA as a joint model | Correction protects the variable; RDA uses `Condition(run)` | Q², driver ASVs (Order-Genus) |
| 8 | Other ML | Do results hold with a different model? Does the microbiome add beyond the environment? | Random Forest (genus level), env-only vs microbiome vs both | Label-free per-run centering | Balanced accuracy, Q², importance |

::: {.callout-note}
## PLS-DA vs PLS for continuous variables
PLS-**DA** is for categories (District). For pH, DO, Temp and Ammonia the matching method is
PLS **regression**: sPLS1 (one variable at a time; best for "which ASVs drive pH") or sPLS2
(all four jointly). Both are in mixOmics and give loadings and VIP scores the same way.
:::

```{r setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(phyloseq)
  library(vegan)
  library(limma)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(ggrepel)
  library(mixOmics)   # loaded after vegan; mixOmics:: prefixes used anyway
  library(cluster)
  library(permute)
})

set.seed(5249)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))

batch_col <- params$batch_col
group_col <- params$group_col
name_col  <- params$name_col
env_vars  <- unlist(params$env_vars)
bc_method <- params$bc_method
```

## Load data and remove the positive control

```{r load}
# setwd("C:/Users/auue0001/OneDrive - Sveriges lantbruksuniversitet/slubi/workshops/ML4LS")

ps <- readRDS(params$ps_path)
# ps <- readRDS("project/dada2_phyloseq.rds")

metadata_df <- as.data.frame(readr::read_delim(params$meta_path, delim = "\t",
                                               escape_double = FALSE, trim_ws = TRUE))
rownames(metadata_df) <- metadata_df$sampleID
sample_data(ps) <- sample_data(metadata_df)

ps <- subset_samples(ps, Group %in% c("1", "2", "3"))   # drop positive control
ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps) > 0, ps)                 # drop ASVs now absent
ps
```

## Short ASV IDs and "Order-Genus" labels

```{r taxonomy}
# ampliseq/DADA2 taxa names are long hashes or sequences: rename to ASV1, ASV2, ...
asv_map <- data.frame(ASV = paste0("ASV", seq_len(ntaxa(ps))), original = taxa_names(ps))
taxa_names(ps) <- asv_map$ASV

tax <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(tax) <- tools::toTitleCase(tolower(names(tax)))   # "genus" -> "Genus"

clean_rank <- function(v) {
  v <- trimws(sub("^[a-zA-Z]__", "", as.character(v)))  # strip SILVA/GTDB "g__" prefixes
  bad <- is.na(v) | v == "" |
    grepl("^(uncultured|unclassified|unknown|metagenome|NA$)", v, ignore.case = TRUE)
  v[bad] <- NA
  v
}
ranks <- intersect(c("Kingdom", "Domain", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus"),
                   names(tax))
for (r in ranks) tax[[r]] <- clean_rank(tax[[r]])
getr <- function(r) if (r %in% names(tax)) tax[[r]] else rep(NA_character_, nrow(tax))

# Order part: Order, else "c_<Class>"; Genus part: Genus, else "f_<Family>"
ord_part <- ifelse(!is.na(getr("Order")), getr("Order"),
                   ifelse(!is.na(getr("Class")), paste0("c_", getr("Class")), "Unclassified"))
gen_part <- ifelse(!is.na(getr("Genus")), getr("Genus"),
                   ifelse(!is.na(getr("Family")), paste0("f_", getr("Family")), "unclassified"))

tax$OrderGenus <- paste(ord_part, gen_part, sep = "-")              # e.g. "Bacillales-Bacillus"
tax$Label      <- paste0(tax$OrderGenus, " (", rownames(tax), ")")   # unique plot label
head(tax[, c("OrderGenus", "Label")])
```

## Count matrix and metadata

```{r matrices}
X_raw <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) X_raw <- t(X_raw)       # samples as rows

meta <- data.frame(sample_data(ps), check.names = FALSE)
meta <- meta[rownames(X_raw), , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(identical(rownames(meta), rownames(X_raw)))

meta[[batch_col]] <- droplevels(factor(meta[[batch_col]]))
meta[[group_col]] <- droplevels(factor(meta[[group_col]]))
meta[[name_col]]  <- factor(meta[[name_col]])
for (v in env_vars) {                        # "7,2" -> 7.2 if read as text
  if (!is.numeric(meta[[v]])) meta[[v]] <- as.numeric(gsub(",", ".", as.character(meta[[v]])))
}

dim(X_raw)
summary(meta[, c(batch_col, group_col, env_vars)])
```

# Sequencing depth

```{r depth-table}
depth <- data.frame(sample = rownames(X_raw),
                    reads  = rowSums(X_raw),
                    nASV   = rowSums(X_raw > 0),
                    meta[, c(batch_col, group_col, name_col)],
                    check.names = FALSE)
summary(depth$reads)
cat("max/min depth ratio:", round(max(depth$reads) / min(depth$reads), 1), "\n")
depth[depth$reads < params$min_depth, ]       # samples below the threshold
```

```{r depth-plots}
#| fig-height: 5
ggplot(depth, aes(reorder(sample, reads), reads, fill = .data[[batch_col]])) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = params$min_depth, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Reads per sample", title = "Library size")

ggplot(depth, aes(.data[[batch_col]], reads, colour = .data[[group_col]])) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_log10() + labs(title = "Library size by run")

# Is depth linked to run or District? (a depth difference by run is part of the batch effect)
anova(lm(as.formula(paste("log10(reads) ~", batch_col, "+", group_col)), data = depth))
```

```{r rarefaction}
# Rarefaction curves: a curve that is still rising at its end = undersampled
rc <- vegan::rarecurve(X_raw, step = max(100, round(min(depth$reads) / 50)), tidy = TRUE)
rc$run <- meta[as.character(rc$Site), batch_col]
ggplot(rc, aes(Sample, Species, group = Site, colour = run)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = min(depth$reads), linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Reads sampled", y = "ASVs observed", title = "Rarefaction curves")

# Slope at the smallest library size: new ASVs per extra read (close to 0 = saturated)
depth$slope_at_min <- vegan::rareslope(X_raw, sample = min(depth$reads))
depth[order(-depth$slope_at_min), c("sample", "reads", "nASV", "slope_at_min")]
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Good's coverage is not informative here
DADA2 removes singletons, so Good's coverage (1 − singletons/reads) is ~1 for every sample.
Use the rarefaction curves and slope instead.
:::

## Alpha diversity at even depth (depth-controlled)

Rarefying is used **only** here. Multivariate analyses use CLR on unrarefied counts.

```{r alpha}
ps_rare <- rarefy_even_depth(ps, sample.size = min(depth$reads), rngseed = 5249,
                             replace = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
alpha <- estimate_richness(ps_rare, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon"))
rownames(alpha) <- sample_names(ps_rare)   # estimate_richness can mangle names (e.g. "X1A")
alpha <- cbind(alpha, meta[rownames(alpha), c(batch_col, group_col)])

ggplot(alpha, aes(.data[[group_col]], Shannon, colour = .data[[batch_col]])) +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_jitter(width = 0.1)) +
  labs(title = paste("Shannon at", min(depth$reads), "reads"))

# District effect adjusted for run (type II: each term after the other)
drop1(lm(as.formula(paste("Shannon ~", group_col, "+", batch_col)), data = alpha), test = "F")
```

# Design check: is run confounded with District?

```{r design-check}
tab <- table(meta[[group_col]], meta[[batch_col]], dnn = c(group_col, batch_col))
tab

chi <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab))
cramer_v <- sqrt(unname(chi$statistic) / (sum(tab) * (min(dim(tab)) - 1)))
cat("Cramér's V (District vs run):", round(cramer_v, 2), "  (0 = balanced, 1 = fully confounded)\n")

# Fully confounded if every District sits in one run, or every run holds one District
fully_confounded <- all(rowSums(tab > 0) == 1) || all(colSums(tab > 0) == 1)
if (fully_confounded) {
  warning("District and run are fully confounded: batch correction would remove the ",
          "District signal. Do NOT correct; analyse within run or report run+District jointly.")
}
```

```{r env-vs-run}
#| fig-height: 4
# Are the measurements themselves different between runs?
env_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(env_vars, function(v)
  data.frame(variable = v, value = meta[[v]], run = meta[[batch_col]],
             group = meta[[group_col]])))
ggplot(env_long, aes(run, value, colour = group)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = batch_col, colour = group_col)

# Share of each variable's variance explained by run (R^2 of lm(var ~ run))
sapply(env_vars, function(v) {
  ok <- !is.na(meta[[v]])
  round(summary(lm(meta[[v]][ok] ~ meta[[batch_col]][ok]))$r.squared, 2)
})
```

::: {.callout-warning}
If a variable's R² with run is close to 1 (e.g. Temp measured once per run), that variable is
confounded with run. Then its microbiome association cannot be separated from the batch
effect, and the sPLS model for it should be reported with that caveat.
:::

# Preprocessing: filtering and CLR

```{r preprocess}
# Keep ASVs with > 0.01% of all reads and present in >= 2 samples
keep <- colSums(X_raw) / sum(X_raw) > 1e-4 & colSums(X_raw > 0) >= 2
X_f  <- X_raw[, keep]
dim(X_f)
cat("Reads retained:", round(100 * sum(X_f) / sum(X_raw), 1), "%\n")

clr <- function(x) { lx <- log(x); lx - rowMeans(lx) }   # samples as rows
clr_raw <- clr(X_f + 1)
```

```{r depth-vs-pc}
# Depth artefact check: does depth correlate with the main axes of variation?
pc_raw <- prcomp(clr_raw)$x[, 1:3]
round(cor(log10(depth$reads), pc_raw, method = "spearman"), 2)
```

# Batch effect

## Helper functions

```{r batch-helpers}
## Batch correction on a CLR matrix (samples x ASVs)
##  limma : removeBatchEffect, protecting `design` (e.g. ~ District) -- uses labels
##  center: subtract each run's mean per ASV                         -- label-free
batch_correct <- function(clr, batch, design = NULL, method = bc_method) {
  batch <- droplevels(factor(batch))
  if (method == "none" || nlevels(batch) < 2) return(clr)
  if (method == "center") {
    out <- clr
    for (b in levels(batch)) {
      i <- batch == b
      out[i, ] <- sweep(clr[i, , drop = FALSE], 2, colMeans(clr[i, , drop = FALSE]))
    }
    return(sweep(out, 2, colMeans(clr), "+"))
  }
  if (method == "limma") {
    if (is.null(design)) design <- matrix(1, nrow(clr), 1)
    full <- cbind(design, model.matrix(~ batch)[, -1, drop = FALSE])
    if (qr(full)$rank < ncol(full)) {
      warning("Batch is confounded with the protected design; returning uncorrected data.")
      return(clr)
    }
    return(t(limma::removeBatchEffect(t(clr), batch = batch, design = design)))
  }
  stop("Unknown method: ", method)
}

## How much variance is batch vs group, before/after correction
batch_metrics <- function(X, meta) {
  vp <- vegan::varpart(X, reformulate(group_col), reformulate(batch_col), data = meta)
  fr <- vp$part$indfract$Adj.R.squared          # [a] group only, [b] batch only, [c] shared
  d  <- dist(X)
  sil <- function(g) mean(cluster::silhouette(as.integer(factor(g)), d)[, "sil_width"])
  data.frame(R2adj_District_only = fr[1], R2adj_run_only = fr[2], R2adj_shared = fr[3],
             silhouette_run = sil(meta[[batch_col]]),
             silhouette_District = sil(meta[[group_col]]))
}

pca_plot <- function(X, title) {
  p  <- prcomp(X)
  ve <- round(100 * p$sdev^2 / sum(p$sdev^2), 1)
  df <- data.frame(p$x[, 1:2], meta[, c(batch_col, group_col)], check.names = FALSE)
  ggplot(df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = .data[[batch_col]], shape = .data[[group_col]])) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", ve[1], "%)"), y = paste0("PC2 (", ve[2], "%)"), title = title)
}
```

## Assess the batch effect (uncorrected data)

```{r batch-assess}
pca_plot(clr_raw, "PCA, CLR, uncorrected")

# PERMANOVA on Aitchison distance: each term adjusted for the other (by = "margin")
d_ait_raw <- dist(clr_raw)
adonis2(as.formula(paste("d_ait_raw ~", group_col, "+", batch_col)),
        data = meta, by = "margin", permutations = 999)

# Variance partitioning: District-only, run-only and shared fractions
vp_raw <- vegan::varpart(clr_raw, reformulate(group_col), reformulate(batch_col), data = meta)
plot(vp_raw, Xnames = c(group_col, batch_col), bg = c("steelblue", "tomato"))
```

## Correct and compare methods

```{r batch-correct}
design_grp <- model.matrix(reformulate(group_col), data = meta)

X_list <- list(
  none   = clr_raw,
  center = batch_correct(clr_raw, meta[[batch_col]], method = "center"),
  limma  = batch_correct(clr_raw, meta[[batch_col]], design = design_grp, method = "limma")
)

## Optional: PLSDA-batch, designed for microbiome data (Wang & Le Cao 2023)
# library(PLSDAbatch)
# pb <- PLSDA_batch(X = clr_raw, Y.trt = meta[[group_col]], Y.bat = meta[[batch_col]],
#                   ncomp.trt = 1, ncomp.bat = 1, balance = FALSE)  # FALSE = weighted, for unbalanced designs
# X_list$plsda_batch <- pb$X.nobatch

bm <- do.call(rbind, lapply(X_list, batch_metrics, meta = meta))
round(bm, 3)
```

```{r batch-pca-after}
#| fig-height: 4
#| layout-ncol: 2
for (m in names(X_list)) print(pca_plot(X_list[[m]], paste("PCA, CLR,", m)))
```

**What a good correction looks like:** `R2adj_run_only` and `silhouette_run` drop toward 0,
while `R2adj_District_only` stays the same or rises.

```{r choose-correction}
X_bc <- X_list[[bc_method]]      # set bc_method in the YAML header
cat("Using batch correction:", bc_method, "\n")
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Which correction to trust
- **limma with District protected** removes run well, but because it uses the District labels,
  District separation on the corrected data is somewhat optimistic when the design is
  unbalanced (Nygaard et al. 2016). The permutation tests below redo the correction for every
  permuted label set, so the p-values stay fair.
- **Per-run centering** uses no labels, so it is safe inside cross-validation, but it removes
  some District signal if Districts are unevenly spread across runs.
- **Statistical tests** (PERMANOVA, RDA) use the uncorrected CLR with run as a term instead of
  corrected data.
:::

# NMDS on District, run and shortName

```{r nmds}
rel <- X_raw / rowSums(X_raw)                     # relative abundance, all ASVs

d_list <- list(
  "Bray-Curtis (raw)"          = vegan::vegdist(rel, method = "bray"),
  "Aitchison (raw)"            = dist(clr_raw),
  "Aitchison (batch-corrected)" = dist(X_bc)
)

set.seed(5249)
nmds_list <- lapply(d_list, function(d) vegan::metaMDS(d, k = 2, trymax = 200, trace = 0))
sapply(nmds_list, function(m) round(m$stress, 3))   # < 0.1 good, 0.1-0.2 fair, > 0.2 poor

nmds_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(nmds_list), function(nm) {
  m <- nmds_list[[nm]]
  data.frame(NMDS1 = m$points[, 1], NMDS2 = m$points[, 2],
             method = paste0(nm, "\nstress = ", round(m$stress, 3)),
             meta[, c(batch_col, group_col, name_col, env_vars)], check.names = FALSE)
}))
```

```{r nmds-plots}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.5
plot_nmds <- function(df, var) {
  shape_var <- if (var == batch_col) group_col else batch_col
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(NMDS1, NMDS2)) + facet_wrap(~ method, scales = "free", nrow = 1)
  if (nlevels(factor(df[[var]])) <= 12) {
    p <- p + geom_point(aes(colour = .data[[var]], shape = .data[[shape_var]]), size = 3)
  } else {                           # many levels (e.g. unique site names): label points
    p <- p + geom_point(aes(colour = .data[[group_col]], shape = .data[[batch_col]]), size = 2.5) +
      ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = .data[[var]]), size = 2.6, max.overlaps = 30)
  }
  p + labs(title = paste("NMDS coloured by", var))
}

plot_nmds(nmds_df, group_col)
plot_nmds(nmds_df, batch_col)
plot_nmds(nmds_df, name_col)
```

## Tests: PERMANOVA and dispersion

```{r nmds-stats}
perm_within_run <- how(nperm = 999, blocks = meta[[batch_col]])

for (nm in names(d_list)[1:2]) {          # tests on raw distances, run in the model
  d <- d_list[[nm]]
  cat("\n=====", nm, "=====\n")
  print(adonis2(as.formula(paste("d ~", group_col, "+", batch_col)),
                data = meta, by = "margin", permutations = 999))
  # District with permutations restricted within run
  print(adonis2(as.formula(paste("d ~", group_col)), data = meta,
                permutations = perm_within_run))
  # shortName only testable if names repeat (replicates)
  if (nlevels(meta[[name_col]]) < nrow(meta)) {
    print(adonis2(as.formula(paste("d ~", name_col)), data = meta, permutations = 999))
  }
  # Homogeneity of dispersion: a significant PERMANOVA can come from spread, not location
  for (g in c(group_col, batch_col)) {
    cat("betadisper:", g, "\n")
    print(permutest(betadisper(d, meta[[g]]), permutations = 999)$tab)
  }
}
```

## Environmental vectors on the corrected NMDS

```{r envfit}
nm_bc <- nmds_list[["Aitchison (batch-corrected)"]]
# permute within run (only possible when no values are missing)
perm_ef <- if (anyNA(meta[, env_vars])) 999 else how(nperm = 999, blocks = meta[[batch_col]])
ef <- vegan::envfit(nm_bc, meta[, env_vars, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE,
                    permutations = perm_ef)
ef

arr <- as.data.frame(scores(ef, display = "vectors"))
arr <- arr * 0.8 * max(abs(nm_bc$points)) / max(abs(as.matrix(arr)))   # scale to plot
arr$var <- rownames(arr)
pts <- nmds_df[grepl("corrected", nmds_df$method), ]

ggplot(pts, aes(NMDS1, NMDS2)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = .data[[group_col]], shape = .data[[batch_col]]), size = 3) +
  geom_segment(data = arr, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = NMDS1, yend = NMDS2),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")), colour = "grey30") +
  geom_text(data = arr, aes(NMDS1 * 1.1, NMDS2 * 1.1, label = var), colour = "grey20") +
  labs(title = "NMDS (Aitchison, corrected) with environmental vectors")
```

# sPLS-DA on District

Input: the batch-corrected CLR matrix `X_bc`. It is already log-ratio transformed, so
`logratio = "none"`. There are no repeated measures (one row per sample), so no `multilevel`.

```{r splsda-setup}
X <- X_bc
Y <- meta[[group_col]]
summary(Y)
n.folds <- min(5, min(table(Y)))    # folds cannot exceed the smallest group
lab <- tax[colnames(X), "Label"]    # "Order-Genus (ASVxx)"
```

```{r plsda-ncomp}
plsda.basic <- mixOmics::plsda(X, Y, ncomp = max(2, nlevels(Y)), logratio = "none")
set.seed(5249)
perf.basic <- mixOmics::perf(plsda.basic, validation = "Mfold", folds = n.folds,
                             nrepeat = 50, progressBar = FALSE)
plot(perf.basic, overlay = "measure", sd = TRUE)
ncomp.perf <- perf.basic$choice.ncomp["BER", "max.dist"]
ncomp.perf
```

```{r splsda-tune}
grid.keepX <- c(seq(5, 50, 5), seq(60, 150, 10))
grid.keepX <- grid.keepX[grid.keepX <= ncol(X)]

set.seed(5249)
tune <- mixOmics::tune.splsda(X, Y, ncomp = max(2, ncomp.perf), logratio = "none",
                              test.keepX = grid.keepX, validation = "Mfold",
                              folds = n.folds, nrepeat = 50, dist = "max.dist",
                              measure = "BER", progressBar = FALSE)
plot(tune)
opt.ncomp <- max(2, tune$choice.ncomp$ncomp)
opt.keepX <- tune$choice.keepX[1:opt.ncomp]
opt.ncomp; opt.keepX
```

```{r splsda-final}
splsda.final <- mixOmics::splsda(X, Y, ncomp = opt.ncomp, keepX = opt.keepX, logratio = "none")

plotIndiv(splsda.final, comp = c(1, 2), ind.names = FALSE, ellipse = TRUE, legend = TRUE,
          legend.title = group_col, title = "sPLS-DA (batch-corrected CLR), comps 1 & 2")

cim(splsda.final, comp = 1:2,
    row.sideColors = color.mixo(as.numeric(Y)),
    legend = list(legend = levels(Y), col = color.mixo(seq_len(nlevels(Y))), title = group_col),
    title = "Selected ASVs")
```

## Cross-validated performance

```{r splsda-perf}
set.seed(5249)
perf.final <- mixOmics::perf(splsda.final, validation = "Mfold", folds = n.folds,
                             nrepeat = 50, dist = "max.dist", progressBar = FALSE)
perf.final$error.rate          # overall error and BER per component
perf.final$error.rate.class    # error per District
cat("Chance-level BER:", round(1 - 1 / nlevels(Y), 2), "\n")
```

## Permutation test

Labels are shuffled **within run**, the batch correction is redone, and the model is refitted
with the same ncomp/keepX. The p-value is the share of permutations with a BER as low as the
real one. (Fixed keepX makes this slightly optimistic; nested tuning is more expensive.)

```{r splsda-perm}
perm_splsda <- function(clr, Y, batch, ncomp, keepX, nperm, folds, nrepeat = 10) {
  fit_ber <- function(Yuse) {
    Xb <- batch_correct(clr, batch, design = model.matrix(~ Yuse))
    m  <- mixOmics::splsda(Xb, Yuse, ncomp = ncomp, keepX = keepX)
    p  <- mixOmics::perf(m, validation = "Mfold", folds = folds, nrepeat = nrepeat,
                         dist = "max.dist", progressBar = FALSE)
    p$error.rate$BER[ncomp, "max.dist"]
  }
  obs  <- fit_ber(Y)
  null <- vapply(seq_len(nperm), function(i)
    fit_ber(Y[permute::shuffle(length(Y), control = how(blocks = batch))]), numeric(1))
  list(observed = obs, null = null, p = (sum(null <= obs) + 1) / (nperm + 1))
}

set.seed(5249)
pt_da <- perm_splsda(clr_raw, Y, meta[[batch_col]], opt.ncomp, opt.keepX,
                     nperm = params$nperm, folds = n.folds)
cat("Observed BER:", round(pt_da$observed, 3), "  permutation p =", signif(pt_da$p, 3), "\n")
hist(pt_da$null, breaks = 20, main = "Null BER (permuted District)", xlab = "BER",
     xlim = range(c(pt_da$null, pt_da$observed)))
abline(v = pt_da$observed, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```

## Leave-one-run-out validation

The strictest check: train on all runs but one, predict the held-out run. Uses label-free
per-run centering, so the held-out run never informs the correction through its labels.

```{r splsda-loro}
loro_splsda <- function(clr, Y, batch, ncomp, keepX) {
  batch <- droplevels(factor(batch))
  Xc    <- batch_correct(clr, batch, method = "center")
  pred  <- rep(NA_character_, length(Y))
  for (b in levels(batch)) {
    te <- batch == b; tr <- !te
    if (nlevels(droplevels(Y[tr])) < nlevels(Y)) {
      message("Run ", b, " skipped: training set lacks some Districts"); next
    }
    ok <- apply(Xc[tr, ], 2, sd) > 1e-8
    m  <- mixOmics::splsda(Xc[tr, ok], droplevels(Y[tr]), ncomp = ncomp,
                           keepX = pmin(keepX, sum(ok)))
    pred[te] <- predict(m, Xc[te, ok, drop = FALSE], dist = "max.dist")$class$max.dist[, ncomp]
  }
  tab <- table(observed = Y, predicted = factor(pred, levels = levels(Y)))
  list(table = tab, BER = mean(1 - diag(tab) / rowSums(tab), na.rm = TRUE))
}

loro <- loro_splsda(clr_raw, Y, meta[[batch_col]], opt.ncomp, opt.keepX)
loro$table
cat("Leave-one-run-out BER:", round(loro$BER, 3), "\n")
```

# sPLS regression on pH, DO, Temp, Ammonia

One sPLS1 model per variable. For each variable:

1. drop samples with a missing value;
2. batch-correct the CLR matrix, protecting that variable (`design = ~ y`);
3. tune ncomp and keepX by leave-one-out Q² (Q² > 0 means better than predicting the mean);
4. permutation test (y shuffled within run, correction and tuning redone);
5. rank driver ASVs by loading, VIP and selection frequency, labelled Order-Genus.

## Environmental variables first

```{r env-cor}
round(cor(meta[, env_vars], use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman"), 2)
pairs(meta[, env_vars], col = as.numeric(meta[[group_col]]), pch = as.numeric(meta[[batch_col]]))
```

## Helper functions

```{r spls-helpers}
## Cross-validated sPLS1; returns Q2, RMSEP, r(pred, obs) and selection frequency
cv_spls1 <- function(X, y, keepX, ncomp = 1, folds = length(y), nrepeat = 1,
                     return_sel = FALSE) {
  n <- length(y)
  pred <- matrix(NA_real_, n, nrepeat)
  sel <- character(0); nfit <- 0
  for (r in seq_len(nrepeat)) {
    fid <- if (folds >= n) seq_len(n) else sample(rep(seq_len(folds), length.out = n))
    for (k in unique(fid)) {
      te <- which(fid == k); tr <- setdiff(seq_len(n), te)
      ok <- apply(X[tr, , drop = FALSE], 2, sd) > 1e-8     # drop constant ASVs in training
      m  <- mixOmics::spls(X[tr, ok, drop = FALSE], y[tr], ncomp = ncomp,
                           keepX = rep(min(keepX, sum(ok)), ncomp), mode = "regression")
      pred[te, r] <- predict(m, newdata = X[te, ok, drop = FALSE])$predict[, 1, ncomp]
      if (return_sel) {
        sel  <- c(sel, mixOmics::selectVar(m, comp = 1)$X$name)
        nfit <- nfit + 1
      }
    }
  }
  tss <- sum((y - mean(y))^2)
  out <- list(Q2    = mean(apply(pred, 2, function(p) 1 - sum((y - p)^2) / tss)),
              RMSEP = mean(apply(pred, 2, function(p) sqrt(mean((y - p)^2)))),
              r     = cor(y, rowMeans(pred)),
              pred  = rowMeans(pred))
  if (return_sel) out$sel_freq <- table(sel) / nfit
  out
}

## Grid search over ncomp x keepX
tune_spls1 <- function(X, y, keepX_grid, ncomp_grid = 1:2) {
  res <- expand.grid(ncomp = ncomp_grid, keepX = keepX_grid[keepX_grid <= ncol(X)])
  cv  <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(res)), function(i) cv_spls1(X, y, res$keepX[i], res$ncomp[i]))
  res$Q2    <- sapply(cv, `[[`, "Q2")
  res$RMSEP <- sapply(cv, `[[`, "RMSEP")
  res$r     <- sapply(cv, `[[`, "r")
  list(table = res, best = res[which.max(res$Q2), ])
}

grid.keepX.reg <- c(5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 50, 75, 100)
```

## Fit, validate and test each variable

```{r spls-run}
set.seed(5249)
reg_res <- lapply(env_vars, function(v) {
  cc <- !is.na(meta[[v]])
  y  <- meta[[v]][cc]
  cl <- clr_raw[cc, ]
  b  <- droplevels(meta[[batch_col]][cc])
  make_X <- function(yy) batch_correct(cl, b, design = model.matrix(~ yy))

  Xv   <- make_X(y)
  tun  <- tune_spls1(Xv, y, grid.keepX.reg)
  best <- tun$best
  cvb  <- cv_spls1(Xv, y, best$keepX, best$ncomp, return_sel = TRUE)

  # Permutation null for Q2 (shuffle within run; redo correction [+ tuning])
  null <- vapply(seq_len(params$nperm), function(i) {
    yp <- y[permute::shuffle(length(y), control = how(blocks = b))]
    Xp <- make_X(yp)
    if (isTRUE(params$perm_tune)) tune_spls1(Xp, yp, grid.keepX.reg)$best$Q2
    else cv_spls1(Xp, yp, best$keepX, best$ncomp)$Q2
  }, numeric(1))

  # Final model on all samples
  fit <- mixOmics::spls(Xv, y, ncomp = best$ncomp, keepX = rep(best$keepX, best$ncomp),
                        mode = "regression")
  vipm <- mixOmics::vip(fit)
  sel  <- mixOmics::selectVar(fit, comp = 1)$X$value
  asv  <- rownames(sel)
  sf   <- cvb$sel_freq

  drivers <- data.frame(
    variable   = v,
    ASV        = asv,
    OrderGenus = tax[asv, "OrderGenus"],
    loading    = sel$value.var,
    VIP        = vipm[asv, best$ncomp],
    sel_freq   = ifelse(asv %in% names(sf), as.numeric(sf[asv]), 0),
    spearman   = sapply(asv, function(a) cor(Xv[, a], y, method = "spearman")),
    tax[asv, intersect(c("Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus"), names(tax))],
    row.names = NULL)
  drivers <- drivers[order(-abs(drivers$loading)), ]

  list(variable = v, n = sum(cc), tuning = tun$table, best = best, cv = cvb,
       null = null, p = (sum(null >= best$Q2) + 1) / (params$nperm + 1),
       y = y, fit = fit, drivers = drivers, samples = rownames(cl))
})
names(reg_res) <- env_vars
```

## Model performance

```{r spls-summary}
reg_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(reg_res, function(r) data.frame(
  variable = r$variable, n = r$n, ncomp = r$best$ncomp, keepX = r$best$keepX,
  Q2 = round(r$best$Q2, 3), RMSEP = signif(r$best$RMSEP, 3), r_pred_obs = round(r$best$r, 2),
  null_Q2_95 = round(quantile(r$null, 0.95), 3), perm_p = signif(r$p, 3))))
reg_summary
write.csv(reg_summary, "sPLS_env_performance.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## How to read this
- **Q² ≤ 0**: the community does not predict the variable better than its mean.
- **Q² > 0 and perm_p < 0.05**: predictive signal; interpret the driver ASVs.
- With `perm_tune: true` the null is tuned the same way as the real model, so it is fair
  even though the best Q² was picked from a grid.
:::

```{r spls-obs-pred}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5
op <- do.call(rbind, lapply(reg_res, function(r)
  data.frame(variable = paste0(r$variable, " (Q2 = ", round(r$best$Q2, 2), ")"),
             observed = r$y, predicted = r$cv$pred,
             run = meta[r$samples, batch_col])))
ggplot(op, aes(observed, predicted, colour = run)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free", nrow = 1) +
  labs(title = "LOO-CV predictions, sPLS1")
```

## Driver × variable heatmap (within-run correlations)

ASVs and environmental variables are both centred within run before correlating, so the
correlations are not driven by run differences.

```{r spls-heatmap}
#| fig-height: 9
top_asv <- unique(unlist(lapply(reg_res, function(r) head(r$drivers$ASV, 15))))
Xc  <- batch_correct(clr_raw, meta[[batch_col]], method = "center")[, top_asv]
Ec  <- sapply(env_vars, function(v) meta[[v]] - ave(meta[[v]], meta[[batch_col]],
                                                    FUN = function(z) mean(z, na.rm = TRUE)))
cmat <- cor(Xc, Ec, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
rownames(cmat) <- tax[top_asv, "Label"]
cmat[is.na(cmat)] <- 0   # a variable constant within every run gives NA
cim(cmat, margins = c(6, 16), title = "Within-run Spearman: driver ASVs vs environment")
```

## Joint model: RDA with run as a conditioning variable

A classical companion to sPLS: how much community variation the four variables explain
together, after removing run.

```{r rda}
cc  <- complete.cases(meta[, env_vars])
Yc  <- clr_raw[cc, ]
env_s <- data.frame(scale(meta[cc, env_vars]), meta[cc, batch_col, drop = FALSE],
                    check.names = FALSE)

rda_env <- vegan::rda(as.formula(paste("Yc ~", paste(env_vars, collapse = " + "),
                                       "+ Condition(", batch_col, ")")), data = env_s)
RsquareAdj(rda_env)
vif.cca(rda_env)                                  # > 10 = collinear variables
anova(rda_env, permutations = 999)                # global test
anova(rda_env, by = "margin", permutations = 999) # each variable given the others
plot(rda_env, display = c("sites", "bp"), main = "Aitchison RDA | run")
```

# Other ML approaches

## Random Forest at genus level

Uses genus-level counts (`Order-Genus`), which are fewer and more robust than ASVs at n = 20,
with label-free per-run centering so leave-one-out CV has no leakage.

```{r rf-features}
library(ranger)
G_raw <- t(rowsum(t(X_raw), group = tax[colnames(X_raw), "OrderGenus"]))   # samples x genera
G_raw <- G_raw[, colSums(G_raw) / sum(G_raw) > 1e-4 & colSums(G_raw > 0) >= 2]
G_bc  <- batch_correct(clr(G_raw + 1), meta[[batch_col]], method = "center")
g_map <- setNames(colnames(G_bc), paste0("G", seq_len(ncol(G_bc))))        # safe names
colnames(G_bc) <- names(g_map)
dim(G_bc)

loo_rf <- function(Xdf, y, num.trees = 1000) {
  pred <- vector("list", length(y))
  for (i in seq_along(y)) {
    m <- ranger::ranger(x = Xdf[-i, , drop = FALSE], y = y[-i], num.trees = num.trees,
                        seed = 5249 + i)
    pred[[i]] <- predict(m, data = Xdf[i, , drop = FALSE])$predictions
  }
  if (is.factor(y)) factor(sapply(pred, as.character), levels = levels(y)) else unlist(pred)
}
bal_acc <- function(obs, pred) { t <- table(obs, pred); mean(diag(t) / rowSums(t)) }
```

```{r rf-district}
# Does the microbiome add beyond the environment? (complete cases only)
cc  <- complete.cases(meta[, env_vars])
Yd  <- droplevels(meta[[group_col]][cc])
sets <- list(
  microbiome  = as.data.frame(G_bc[cc, ]),
  environment = meta[cc, env_vars, drop = FALSE],
  both        = cbind(as.data.frame(G_bc[cc, ]), meta[cc, env_vars, drop = FALSE])
)
rf_district <- sapply(sets, function(s) round(bal_acc(Yd, loo_rf(s, Yd)), 2))
rf_district
cat("Chance balanced accuracy:", round(1 / nlevels(Yd), 2), "\n")

# Permutation importance from the full microbiome model
rf_full <- ranger::ranger(x = as.data.frame(G_bc), y = meta[[group_col]], num.trees = 2000,
                          importance = "permutation", seed = 5249)
imp <- sort(rf_full$variable.importance, decreasing = TRUE)[1:20]
data.frame(OrderGenus = g_map[names(imp)], importance = round(imp, 4), row.names = NULL)
```

```{r rf-env}
# RF regression for each environmental variable (LOO Q2), to compare with sPLS
rf_env <- sapply(env_vars, function(v) {
  ok <- !is.na(meta[[v]])
  y  <- meta[[v]][ok]
  p  <- loo_rf(as.data.frame(G_bc[ok, ]), y)
  round(1 - sum((y - p)^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2), 3)
})
data.frame(variable = env_vars, Q2_RF = rf_env, Q2_sPLS = reg_summary$Q2)
```

## Further suggestions

| Method | Why it fits this study | R package |
|---|---|---|
| **Log-ratio signatures** (balances) | Finds a small set of taxa ratios that predict the outcome; built for compositional data and small n; very interpretable | `coda4microbiome`, `selbal` |
| **Elastic net** with nested CV | Sparse linear baseline for District and env variables; compare to sPLS | `glmnet`, `mikropml` |
| **Differential abundance with run as covariate** | Confirms sPLS/RF driver taxa with a formal model (`~ District + run`, `~ pH + run`) | `ANCOMBC` (ANCOM-BC2), `Maaslin3`, `LinDA` (`MicrobiomeStat`) |
| **Count-level batch correction** | Corrects counts (not CLR), so Bray–Curtis and DA tools can use corrected data | `ConQuR`, `MMUPHin` |
| **Mixed models for alpha diversity** | `Shannon ~ District + (1 | run)` treats run as random | `lme4`, `glmmTMB` |
| **SHAP for the RF model** | Per-sample explanation of which genera push predictions | `kernelshap` + `shapviz` |
| **Genus vs ASV sensitivity** | Rerun sPLS-DA on `G_bc`; drivers that appear at both levels are more convincing | – |
| **Sample-size planning** | The permutation nulls show the effect size you can detect; use them to argue for more samples per District/run | – |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Reporting checklist
- State the batch correction used and show the before/after variance partitioning.
- Report CV error **and** permutation p-values for every supervised model; treat
  leave-one-run-out as the most realistic estimate.
- Call driver ASVs "associated with", not "causing", the outcome.
:::
